---
title: "Figure 3.1: Terms of Trade"
---

![Python: `python/fig-3-1.py`](../images/python/fig-3-1.png)

Annual terms-of-trade indices for five economies, with 2019 = 100. The terms
of trade are the price of a country's exports relative to the price of its
imports. Above 100 means that exports buy more imports than in 2019; below
100, fewer. All five lines therefore start at the same point, and the chart
is about how far they move apart.

**New in this chart:**

- years used directly as x-values;
- an axis line at 100 instead of zero.

## The data

Sheet `data`, 8 rows (2019 to 2026):

| category | USA | CAN | LA7 | CAPDR | CARIB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2019 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 | 100 |

The first row is 100 for every series, as it should be for an index with
2019 as its base year. Checking this is a quick test that the right data
were extracted.

## The script

### The colours and the frame

```python
series_colours = {
    "USA": "#0067A5",
    "CAN": "#454545",
    "LA7": "#5C277E",
    "CAPDR": "#D26717",
    "CARIB": "#00A3A3",
}
```

One entry per line, in drawing and legend order. The colours follow the
REO's usual assignment: blue for the United States, dark grey for Canada,
purple for LA7, orange for CAPDR and teal for the Caribbean. The same
colours appear for these groups throughout the book.

`new_chart()` is called with `caption_size=8.4`, slightly below the default,
so the longest caption line fits.

### An axis line at 100

```python
years = data["category"]

# The x-axis is drawn at 100, with short tick marks pointing up.
ax.axhline(100, color="#222222", linewidth=0.7)
ax.vlines(years, 100, 100.45, color="#222222", linewidth=0.6)
```

For an index, the base value plays the role that zero plays for a growth
rate: it separates "better than in 2019" from "worse". In Excel, the axis
option *Horizontal axis crosses at 100* draws the axis line there, with its
tick marks, while the y-scale starts lower, at 90.

matplotlib has no such option, so the script draws the line and its tick
marks itself:

- `ax.axhline(100, ...)` draws a horizontal line across the whole plot at
  y = 100. Unlike `ax.plot()`, it needs no x-values: it always spans the
  full width, whatever the x-limits.
- `ax.vlines(x, ymin, ymax, ...)` draws vertical lines. Here it draws one
  short line at each year, from 100 to 100.45. These are the tick marks.
  Their length is in data units (0.45 index points), which on this scale
  comes out at about the length of the normal tick marks.

Both are drawn before the series lines, so the series lie on top of them.
See [An axis line at zero, with tick
marks](../techniques.qmd#sec-axis-line).

### The lines and the x-axis

```python
for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    ax.plot(years, data[series], color=colour, linewidth=1.7,
            solid_capstyle="round", solid_joinstyle="round", label=series)

ax.set_xlim(2018.5, 2026.5)
ax.set_xticks(years)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=2.3, pad=5)
```

The years are numbers, so they are plotted directly. There is no need for
positions 0, 1, 2, ... as in [Figure 1.1](fig-1-1.qmd), where the
categories are text such as "2023Q1".

- **Rounded lines.** `solid_capstyle="round"` and
  `solid_joinstyle="round"` round the ends and the corners of the lines.
  Five lines starting from the same point look cleaner that way. See [Line
  styles](../techniques.qmd#sec-line-styles).
- **The limits** are half a year beyond the first and last year, as Excel
  leaves for a category axis.
- **Every year gets a label**, because `ax.set_xticks(years)` puts a tick at
  each value of the column. With eight years there is room for all of them.

### The y-axis and the legend

```python
ax.set_ylim(90, 125)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(5))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.3, pad=5)

ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.03, 0.99), fontsize=9.5,
          handlelength=3.0, labelspacing=0.1)
```

The y-axis runs from 90 to 125 with a tick every 5. `MultipleLocator(5)`
puts a tick at every multiple of 5, like Excel's *major unit*. See [Number
formats and tick spacing](../techniques.qmd#sec-number-formats).

The legend sits in the top-left corner, above the lines. It uses a slightly
larger font (9.5 instead of 9 points) and close line spacing
(`labelspacing=0.1`), so five entries fit in the space above the lines. See
[Legends](../techniques.qmd#sec-legends).

## Changing the chart

- **A different base year.** If the next edition uses 2020 = 100, change the
  subtitle. The axis line stays at 100, because the base value is still
  100, but check the y-limits, since the lines will move.
- **An index with no special line.** Delete the `axhline` and `vlines`
  calls. The x-axis is then the bottom edge of the plot, at 90.
- **More years.** Once there are more than about ten, label every second
  year: `ax.set_xticks(years[::2])`.

## The complete script

The full `python/fig-3-1.py`, as it runs:

```` {.python filename="python/fig-3-1.py"}
"""Figure 3.1: Terms of Trade."""
from matplotlib.ticker import MultipleLocator

from chart_style import new_chart, read_chart_data, save_chart

STEM = "fig-3-1"

data = read_chart_data(STEM)

series_colours = {
    "USA": "#0067A5",
    "CAN": "#454545",
    "LA7": "#5C277E",
    "CAPDR": "#D26717",
    "CARIB": "#00A3A3",
}

fig, ax = new_chart(
    title="Terms of Trade",
    subtitle="(Index: 2019 = 100)",
    caption=(
        "Sources: IMF, World Economic Outlook database; and IMF staff\n"
        "calculations.\n"
        "Note: Aggregates are purchasing-power-parity GDP-weighted averages.\n"
        "CAPDR = Central America, Panama, and the Dominican Republic; CARIB\n"
        "= Caribbean; LA7 = Latin America 7 (Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico,\n"
        "Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay)."
    ),
    caption_size=8.4,
    left=0.4,
    right=0.15,
    bottom_gap=0.35,
)

years = data["category"]

# The x-axis is drawn at 100, with short tick marks pointing up.
ax.axhline(100, color="#222222", linewidth=0.7)
ax.vlines(years, 100, 100.45, color="#222222", linewidth=0.6)

for series, colour in series_colours.items():
    ax.plot(years, data[series], color=colour, linewidth=1.7,
            solid_capstyle="round", solid_joinstyle="round", label=series)

ax.set_xlim(2018.5, 2026.5)
ax.set_xticks(years)
ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=2.3, pad=5)

ax.set_ylim(90, 125)
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(MultipleLocator(5))
ax.tick_params(axis="y", length=2.3, pad=5)

ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(0.03, 0.99), fontsize=9.5,
          handlelength=3.0, labelspacing=0.1)

save_chart(fig, STEM)
````
